metadata.title: ListenLoop
metadata.description: English listening practice: master one clip a week. Dictate on Day 1, shadow on Days 2–6, and see your progress on Day 7. Official lessons are free.

home.tagline: Master one English clip a week. Hear every word.

intro.title: How it works: a seven-day loop

day1.title: Day 1 Dictation
day1.body: Listen sentence by sentence and type what you hear; see your mistakes right away, then read the handout.

days2to6.title: Days 2–6 Shadowing
days2to6.body: Say every sentence after the audio each day; speech recognition shows the words you missed.

day7.body: Take the same dictation again and compare it with Day 1 to see your progress.

pixelFish.intro: Style: realistic colors, big cute eyes. True-to-life patterns, colors, and light; eyes about 1/3 of the head’s height with one big and one small glint; a slightly rounder, shorter body. They blink now and then and look at the pointer or food; happy ^ ^ after eating; hungry with half-closed lids, slower and lower. Colors, eye size, and other knobs live in lib/pixel-fish/style.ts.

pixelFish.reduced: Reduced motion is on: the fish stays still, doesn’t blink, and its eyes don’t move. The buttons switch still expressions.
pixelFish.lookHint: Move the pointer or a finger over the tank and the fish looks at it; it watches food as it sinks.
pixelFish.togetherHint: From small to big: snail < clownfish < great white < whale shark. The whale shark is the slowest; the snail creeps along the glass and the floor.
pixelFish.togetherLabel: A snail, a clownfish, a great white, and a whale shark in one pixel-art aquarium
pixelFish.snailNote: Eyes on the tentacle tips; a shell with a logarithmic spiral; creeps along the glass and the floor.
pixelFish.clownfishNote: Three white bands edged in black, black fin margins.
pixelFish.greatWhiteNote: Still a shark: pointed snout, grey back and white belly, gill slits, tall dorsal fin, crescent tail; short and chubby with a little toothy smile.
pixelFish.whaleSharkNote: The biggest and slowest: a broad flat head with a wide front mouth, white spots and faint stripes, white belly.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: ListenLoop is an English listening practice site. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, where it's kept, and how you can delete it. Every practice feature works without signing in.

sections.title: What we collect
paragraphs: Only when you sign in (Google, LINE, or email) do we collect the following:
items: Account details from how you sign in: from Google, your email, name, picture URL, and account ID; from LINE, your email, display name, and LINE user ID; with email sign-up, your email and password. Supabase stores the password hashed, so we never see it. Only the email is shown on screen.
One account: whichever way you sign in, one email is one account, and your progress is combined.
Practice data: your progress on each video (which days are done, dictation answers and accuracy, shadowing status) and a daily practice log.
Created practices: the text you type or upload when creating a practice, its sentences and translations, the vocabulary and grammar notes, and the generated audio.

Sharing and reports: anyone can see a public practice's title, sentences, translations, notes, and audio, but not its author's account details. When you report a practice, we keep the reason, your details, and your account ID only to review it; the author isn't told who reported it.
Sign-in state: a sign-in token in a browser cookie.

Account data: the user number the system gives you, your role (user or admin), account status, and when you joined and were last active. The admin pages identify users by number and don’t show emails.

Activity log: events such as signing in, starting a practice, completing a day (with its score), retrying, creating, editing, deleting, or publishing a practice, reporting, skipping a sentence, speech recognition failures, and deleting your account. Only your user number and the needed fields (practice code, day, score, a short code) are kept — never practice text, recognized speech, or recordings.

Hard-sentence reports: when shadowing one sentence stays under half five times in a row and you choose “Try again” or “Skip and report,” we keep the sentence’s position, each try’s coverage, the text speech recognition heard, your browser and system names, and whether you skipped; and, if you’re signed in, your account. Text only, never audio. You can report without signing in, in which case no account is kept.
Feedback: what you send us, and (if signed in) your account.

sections.title: When you're not signed in
paragraphs: Your progress stays in your browser (localStorage) and is never sent to our servers. The interface language is kept in a cookie and the theme in localStorage. Clearing your browser data removes them.

sections.title: How we use it
paragraphs: Only to sign you in and keep your progress in sync across devices. We don't sell data, share it with advertisers, or use advertising or analytics trackers.

sections.title: Where it's kept and who processes it
items: Supabase: the database for accounts and cloud practice data, in the United States (us-east-1).
Vercel: the web host, which handles the technical data a connection needs (such as IP addresses) to serve and protect the site.
Google: Google sign-in.

Microsoft Azure AI services: when you create a practice, its text is sent to Azure OpenAI (the gpt-5-mini model) to split it into sentences, translate it, and write vocabulary and grammar notes, or to write practice text for the situation you pick; its English sentences go to Azure Speech for audio. Under Microsoft's terms, what's sent and what's generated aren't used to train models. Azure OpenAI may keep them for up to 30 days to detect abuse, and may process them in any of Microsoft's regions (a Global Standard deployment); Azure Speech processes them in the United Arab Emirates. Even so, please don't put personal or sensitive information in practice text.
YouTube: practice videos play through YouTube (youtube-nocookie.com); once a video plays, YouTube may set cookies under Google's privacy policy.

Speech recognition: shadowing uses your browser's built-in speech recognition; in Chrome, audio is sent to Google's servers to be recognized. ListenLoop doesn't record or store audio, only whether each sentence is done and how much was heard.
LINE (LY Corporation): when you sign in with LINE, it handles the sign-in and gives us your account details.

sections.title: Payment data
paragraphs: When you subscribe to the paid plan, payments are handled by a third-party payment service (not open yet). It collects and keeps your card and payment details; ListenLoop never sees or stores your full card number.

We keep only what the subscription needs: the plan, billing period, next payment date, and each payment's amount, currency, date, and status (paid or refunded), to provide the paid features, show your payment history, handle refunds, and keep transaction records as the law requires. Deleting your account deletes these too, except records the law requires us to keep.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Your account and practice data are kept while your account exists. The activity log is kept 180 days and hard-sentence reports 365 days, then deleted automatically. The API usage log (number of calls, tokens, characters, estimated cost — no text) is kept to account for service costs; deleting your account removes its link to you. When you delete your account, your account, practices, activity, reports, and feedback are deleted from the database right away; audio files of your practices are deleted too, unless another practice shares them. Service providers’ system backups are cleared when their retention ends.

sections.title: Your choices and rights
items: You can sign out at any time; your practice data stays on this device.
On the Account page you can download your data (JSON): your account data, cloud progress, the practices you made, your activity, reports, and feedback.
On the Account page you can permanently delete your account and cloud data, which also clears the practice data on this device.
To see, correct, or delete your data, or with any other privacy question, contact us through “Feedback” at the bottom of the page.

sections.title: Young users
paragraphs: ListenLoop is mainly for high school and university students. If you’re under 18, use it with the consent of a parent or guardian who has read this policy. If you’re under 13, don’t create an account yourself. When you create a practice of your own, the text you type or upload is sent to AI services to be processed (see above), so don’t include personal information.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: When this policy changes, we update this page and the date above. Major changes are also announced on the site.

accentNotes.us: The most common standard accent, with a clear r sound.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: Welcome to ListenLoop (the “Service”), a seven-day loop for English listening practice. By using the Service you agree to these terms; if you don’t, please stop using it.

sections.title: 1. What the Service is
paragraphs: The Service offers dictation, shadowing, and bilingual handouts, with built-in public-domain or Creative Commons material, ListenLoop’s official materials, and practices that users share publicly (shared materials). You can practice built-in and official materials without signing in; signing in syncs your progress across devices.
Some content (such as the English text, translations, vocabulary and grammar notes, and voices of official materials) is made by AI and may contain mistakes; treat it as a learning aid.

sections.title: 2. Accounts
paragraphs: You can sign in with Google, LINE, or an email and password; one email is one account whichever way you use. Keep your password safe and don’t reuse it on other sites; you’re responsible for activity on your account. If you’re under 18, use the service with the consent of a parent or guardian who has read these terms and the privacy policy; if you’re under 13, please don’t create an account.

sections.title: 3. Rules
paragraphs: When using the Service, don’t:
items: upload or share content that infringes copyright, trademarks, or other rights;
upload personal data, confidential information, or illegal, harassing, hateful, sexual, or violent content;
impersonate others, or access, disrupt, or attack the Service in bulk or by automated means;
get around the Service’s usage limits or security;
use the Service for anything illegal.

sections.title: 4. Content you upload
paragraphs: Text you type or upload to make a practice stays yours or its rights holder’s. You must have the right to use it and are responsible for it.

To run the Service, you let ListenLoop store, process (including sending it to AI services for translations, notes, and voices), and display it; when you make a practice public, you also let other users view and practice it. You can make it private again or delete it at any time, after which we stop offering it.

sections.title: 5. Reports and takedowns
paragraphs: If you believe a public practice infringes your rights or is inappropriate, use “Report” on its page or tell us through “Feedback” at the bottom of the page, saying which practice and why.

We review every report and take the practice down when needed; its author sees the reason in My materials. An author who thinks a takedown is mistaken can explain through Feedback, and we’ll review it again. Accounts that break the rules repeatedly may be disabled.

sections.title: 6. Exam-style materials
paragraphs: Materials labeled “TOEFL-style,” “IELTS-style,” “TOEIC-style,” or “GEPT-style” imitate the format and difficulty only. Their content is original, not real test items, and the Service has no partnership with or license from the test makers.

sections.title: 7. Paid plan and subscriptions
paragraphs: Paid plans (Plus, Pro) are subscriptions billed monthly or yearly, at the prices on the Plans and pricing page. A yearly plan’s allowance resets every month and doesn’t carry over. A third-party payment service handles payment.

Shared materials (practices other users share) can be practiced in full on Plus, Pro, and class plans; on the free plan or signed out, you can preview the first three sentences and listen to the first. You can always practice the materials you share yourself. A shared material you were already practicing when this rule began can be finished for that week.

Subscriptions renew automatically: at the end of each period, your payment method is charged for the next, until you cancel. Cancel any time on the Account page; you keep the paid plan until the period ends.

Refunds follow the refund policy: a full refund within 7 days of the first payment; a yearly plan ended early refunds its unused whole months. If prices change, we’ll tell you before the next period starts, and you can cancel before the change applies.
When a subscription ends or you return to the free plan, your materials and progress are kept; you just can't add new materials.

sections.title: 8. Disclaimer
paragraphs: The Service is provided “as is.” We work to keep it running and its content accurate, but we don’t promise it will be uninterrupted or error-free, or any learning result or test score. Speech recognition depends on your browser and surroundings and is only a practice aid.
As far as the law allows, we aren’t liable for indirect losses from using or being unable to use the Service.

sections.title: 9. Changes to the Service
paragraphs: We may add, change, or stop features, or change usage limits. If these terms are broken, we may disable accounts or remove content. You can delete your account at any time on the Account page.

sections.title: 10. Changes to these terms
paragraphs: When these terms change, we update this page and the date above, and announce major changes on the site. Using the Service after a change means you accept the new terms.

sections.title: 11. Governing law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the laws of the Republic of China (Taiwan).

refund.title: Refund policy
refund.intro: ListenLoop's paid plan is a digital service that renews automatically. This page explains how to cancel and when you can get a refund.

sections.title: 1. Cancelling renewal
paragraphs: Cancel any time under Plan and payments on the Account page. You won't be charged again; the paid plan lasts until the current period ends, then returns to Free.

sections.title: 2. Full refund within 7 days
paragraphs: Within 7 days of your first payment (monthly or yearly), you can ask for a full refund, no reason needed. The paid plan ends when it’s refunded.

sections.title: 3. Ending a yearly plan early
paragraphs: After 7 days, you can still end a yearly plan early: the unused whole months are refunded at that plan’s own monthly rate (for example, Plus yearly at NT$1,490 used for 3 months and a few days refunds 8 × NT$1,490 ÷ 12 ≈ NT$993). The month already started isn’t refunded.
A yearly plan’s allowance still resets every month; unused minutes don’t carry over or turn into refunds.

sections.title: 4. Later payments
paragraphs: Renewal payments generally aren't refunded. If you forgot to cancel and haven't created a material with the paid plan this period, ask within 7 days of the payment and we'll look at it.

sections.title: 5. How to ask
paragraphs: Use Feedback at the bottom of any page, with your account's email and the payment date. We reply within 5 working days. Refunds go back to the original payment method; how long they take depends on your bank or payment service.

sections.title: 6. Your materials after a downgrade
paragraphs: Back on the free plan, your materials and progress are kept and you can keep practicing; you just can't add new materials.

sections.title: 7. Purchases through Google Play
paragraphs: If you subscribed in the Android app through Google Play, cancelling and refunds follow Google Play’s rules. Google Play offers monthly and yearly too.

learn.indexIntro: Choose a topic. Every material follows the 7-day loop: dictation on Day 1, shadowing on Days 2–6, dictation again on Day 7 to see your progress. Official materials are free.

intros.daily-life: Ordering food, shopping, asking the way, booking a doctor: everyday English for home and abroad. Each material is a short, realistic dialogue or talk; spend 7 days hearing every word.
intros.travel: Checking in at the airport and hotel, taking trains, asking the way, ordering: the English you meet most when traveling. Hear it first, then say it, and speak up with confidence.
intros.study-abroad: Housing, bank accounts, roommates, talking to professors: the English international students meet in their first year. Practice before you go.
intros.casual-american: How Americans really talk, with linking and dropped sounds: spoken English you hear in films but rarely in textbooks. Catch every word of fast conversation.
intros.campus: Choosing courses, class discussions, the library, office hours: English on a university campus, for students heading abroad or in English-taught classes.
intros.academic-writing: Research proposals, abstracts, peer review, presentations: academic English to listen to. Get used to formal wording and long sentences.
intros.business: Meetings, calls, emails, and presentations: the English used most at work. Short materials to catch every word from colleagues and clients.
intros.news: Short news rewritten from public-domain releases and original news-style stories: science, environment, health, and life. Get used to news pace and wording.
intros.science: Space, climate, psychology, nutrition: science explained in plain English. Practice listening while learning something new.
intros.talks-stories: Talks, stories, podcast interviews, and book reviews: longer English with more rise and fall. Keep up with the speaker's rhythm and points.
intros.health: Doctor's visits, pharmacies, describing symptoms, appointments: health English, the kind you most need to hear clearly abroad.
intros.relationships: Family, friends, roommates: invitations, apologies, comfort, and discussions. Hear the tone and the details of how people talk.
intros.tech: Phones, the internet, account settings, and tech news: the technology English that's everywhere now.
intros.money-admin: Bank accounts, bills, leases, and paperwork: English where numbers and details are easy to miss. Hear every word and get things done.
intros.career: Job interviews, internships, salary talks, and career plans: the English you most need to understand when looking for work.
intros.leisure: Sports, the gym, signing up for classes, weekend plans: relaxed English for free time.
intros.food: Ordering, recipes, markets, and table manners: English about food.
intros.culture: Festivals, traditions, and cultures around the world: learn about the English-speaking world while you practice.
intros.exam: Original practice in the style of the TOEFL, IELTS, TOEIC, and GEPT (not real test questions). Seven days with one material to hear every word of each task type.
